stem: What is the core idea of object-oriented programming?
options: Objects bundle data together with the rules that protect it
explanation: An object owns its data AND the methods that guard it - so the data cannot be put into an impossible state from outside.

stem: Three parallel arrays (titles[], isOnLoan[], borrowers[]) share an index. What is the danger?
options: Sort or edit one and the data silently corrupts - nothing keeps them in step
explanation: Nothing enforces that index 3 in each array describes the same book. One sort, insert or typo and the data is scrambled with no error. A class keeps the facts together.

stem: Reading a brief, what do the NOUNS usually become?
explanation: Nouns suggest classes, verbs suggest methods, adjectives and values suggest properties. It is a starting point, not a law - some nouns turn out to be properties.

stem: Which is NOT one of the four pillars of OOP?
explanation: The four pillars are abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism. Compilation is how any C# runs, OOP or not.

stem: In the LibraryBook class, why is _borrower private?
options: So nobody outside can forge or corrupt a loan - all changes go through Lend and Return
explanation: The only way in is through methods that enforce the rules - a book already on loan refuses a second borrower. That is the entire point of the design.

stem: Which task LEAST needs a class?
options: A game with players and enemies
explanation: A short script gains ceremony and no protection from a class. OOP earns its keep when there is state with rules attached.

stem: A class named DataManagerHelper is usually a sign of what?
options: A verb pretending to be a noun - the real object has not been found
explanation: Manager, Helper, Processor and Data are what you name a class when you have not identified the actual thing. Look again for the real noun.

stem: What kind of language is C#?
options: Multi-paradigm: OO at heart, with functional and procedural styles available
explanation: LINQ is functional in style, static helper classes are procedural, and classes are OO. Use whichever fits the problem.

stem: Fines are calculated in one Loan class. The fine rate changes. What needs editing?
explanation: Localising change is a core OOP payoff: one fact lives in one place, so one change touches one class.

stem: What is the relationship between a class and an object?
options: A class is a blueprint; an object is one thing built from it
A class is one instance of an object
explanation: One Book class; ten thousand Book objects, each with its own title and state.
